question: Locate the anchor function for the browser_fingerprint field in the console.log object whose action is account.submit after filling the probe label, clicking Prepare, and clicking Collect on the page. The anchor function is the first target-specific browser fingerprint value constructor on the dynamic behavior chain: after the arming event, scan-button routing, runtime state collection, multi-layer route progression, browser capability-surface collection and input preparation, its function body itself constructs the target observable browser fingerprint digest value rather than merely collecting raw navigator/screen/canvas features, dispatching control, wrapping a return value, or writing to the console. Return exactly one complete function as a single JSON object (see answer_format). Do not return generic utilities, event handlers, the full call chain, raw feature collectors, or the final sink. Note: you may only inspect code under captures; the full codebase is not accessible.

function_name.description: The identifier on the function declaration line in the captured bundle slice (the name immediately after the `function` keyword). Use the name as it appears in captures, not a guessed source-level name.

file.description: Path to the JavaScript file under captures/ that contains the function. Must match visible_corpus.

slice.description: One contiguous source slice covering exactly one complete function body in the captured bundle.

start_line.description: 1-based inclusive start line of the function in file.

end_line.description: 1-based inclusive end line of the function in file.

start_offset.description: 0-based byte offset in file where the function slice begins.

end_offset.description: 0-based byte offset in file where the function slice ends (exclusive).

code.description: Exact source text of the complete function from start_offset to end_offset. Must start with `function <function_name>(` and end with the closing brace of that function.

public_constraints: Only code visible under captures is in scope.
Submit exactly one JSON object matching answer_format.response_schema; do not wrap it in markdown fences unless the evaluation harness explicitly requires that.
function_name and slice.code must refer to the same function declaration in the captured bundle.
slice.code must be one complete function (balanced braces), not a signature fragment, partial body, or multiple functions.
Return one top-1 function, not a list of candidate chains.
Do not return the final console sink.
Do not return a generic DOM reader, router, payload wrapper or raw browser-feature collector when a more target-specific fingerprint value constructor is present.
Constrain the observable by both action and field.
The target value is a browser fingerprint digest and should not be confused with device_hash, browser_trace or non-target browser_fingerprint-like decoys.
